crossrefs.anchor: Does not wisdom call out, and understanding raise her voice?
Beside the gates to the city, at the entrances she cries out:
“To you, O men, I call out, and my cry is to the sons of men.
O simple ones, learn to be shrewd; O fools, gain understanding.
for I speak of noble things
the opening of my lips
my mouth will speak the truth
detestable to
All the words of my mouth are righteous
none are crooked or perverse
They are all plain to the discerning, and upright to those who find knowledge.
Receive my instruction instead of silver, and knowledge rather than pure gold.
wisdom
I, wisdom
knowledge and discretion
To fear the LORD
arrogant pride
perverse speech
Counsel
sound judgment
I have insight and strength
By me
enact just laws
I love those who love me
those who seek me early shall find me
riches and honor
enduring wealth
and righteousness
My fruit is better than gold, pure gold, and my harvest surpasses choice silver.
walk in the way of righteousness
along the paths of justice
bestowing wealth on those who love me
making their treasuries full
The LORD created me as His first course, before His works of old.
From everlasting I was established, from the beginning, before the earth began.
I was brought forth
Before the mountains were settled, before the hills, I was brought forth,
before He made the land or fields
when He established the heavens
when He inscribed a circle
when He set a boundary for the sea
when He marked out the foundations of the earth
a skilled craftsman at His side
His delight day by day
delighting together in the sons of men
for blessed are those who keep my ways
Listen to instruction
do not ignore it
watching daily at my doors
For whoever finds me finds life
obtains the favor of the LORD
But he who fails to find me harms himself
all who hate me love death

evidence.text: To fear the LORD is to hate evil; I hate arrogant pride, evil conduct, and perverse speech.
The LORD created me as His first course, before His works of old.
For whoever finds me finds life and obtains the favor of the LORD.

matchReviews.senseReview: Only literal uppercase LORD is admitted globally. Source Lord article explicitly covers God as Lord; lowercase human lord and sentence-title Lord are not inferred from this rule.
